faq: Do you need the source code?
Not for Basic or Standard. We review the app from the outside, through a TestFlight build or the App Store version. Premium includes code review, so we need read-only access to your repository.
Will you fix the problems you find?
The audit is the review and the plan. We can fix issues through our feature work or maintenance services, and Premium lists priced options so you can decide what to hire out.
Do you check for App Store rejection risks?

We check against Apple's published App Review Guidelines, such as privacy, payments, permissions and metadata. Apple makes the final decision on any app, so we flag risks rather than promise outcomes.
Can you audit an app that is not yet released?
Yes. Send a TestFlight invite and we review the build the same way. It is a good moment to find problems before reviewers or customers do.
desc:
An iOS app audit and review from Ecom Swift LLC gives you an honest, written picture of how your iPhone app works today: what crashes, what feels slow, what confuses new users and what could trouble App Review. You get a prioritized fix list, so you know what to repair first.

## What is an iOS app audit?

An iOS app audit is a structured review of a finished or nearly finished iPhone app, carried out by someone who did not build it. The reviewer installs the app, uses it like a new customer and, if you share the code, reads the main modules. The result is a report that lists each problem, explains its effect and suggests a fix.

An audit does not change your app. It tells you where the real risks and the cheapest improvements are, before you spend money on the wrong work.

## Why an outside review matters

Teams get used to their own app. They know which button to tap, which screen to skip and which crash to ignore. A new user knows none of that. They meet a confusing first screen, a button that sits too close to the edge on a small phone, or a permission request that arrives before they understand why.

Without a review, these problems show up as one-star ratings, deleted apps and rejected submissions. An audit gathers them in one place while they are still cheap to fix.

## How an audit affects retention, ratings and approval

People rarely complain about small friction. They simply leave. A crash on launch, a slow list or a form that loses typed text each cost you a user who does not come back, and they also lower the ratings that new visitors read on your App Store page.

Fixing problems in order of impact matters more than fixing everything. A sorted list lets you remove the issues that hurt the most users first. A check against the App Review Guidelines lowers the chance of a rejected update, though only Apple decides on approval.

## What a thorough audit covers

- Stability: crash logs, hangs and screens that freeze under poor network conditions.
- Speed: launch time, scrolling in long lists, image loading and memory use.
- Layout: how screens look on small and large iPhones, in landscape and with larger text.
- Accessibility: VoiceOver labels, contrast, tap target size and Dynamic Type.
- User flow: sign-up, first use, empty states, error messages and the way back out of each screen.
- App Store rules: privacy labels, permission wording, purchase flows and account deletion.
- Code health: structure of key modules, outdated libraries and risky patterns, when code is shared.
- Security and privacy: how data is stored, sent and logged.
- Effort notes: a rough size for each fix, so you can plan the work.

## How we run the audit

We start with the build you give us, through TestFlight or the App Store, and use it on real devices and simulators. We note every issue with a screenshot or a short description, then sort the list by effect on users and by effort to fix.

The Basic package covers the main flows and the top issues. Standard goes further into design, speed and App Review Guidelines, and includes a walkthrough call. Premium covers the whole app, adds code reading and a privacy checklist, and ends with a longer call and a fix plan with options. We report only what we can see and test.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us the three things you worry about most before we start.
- Share crash reports or analytics if you have them.
- Give us a test account with sample data so we can see every screen.
- Use the walkthrough call to ask about trade-offs.
- Decide on an order of fixes before you brief developers.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing issues before you have seen the whole list.
- Hiding known problems, which only makes the report less useful.
- Treating an audit as proof of approval or good ratings.
- Asking for a code review without sharing the code.
- Letting the report sit unread while new releases keep adding changes.

## Who needs an audit

A founder who inherited an app from a previous agency often wants to know what state it is really in. A product owner with falling ratings needs to find the cause before briefing a developer. A team preparing a major release may want a second pair of eyes on the riskiest screens and on App Review Guidelines.

An audit also suits buyers who are about to acquire an app and want a clear view of its quality first.

## What we need from you

Send us a TestFlight invitation or the App Store link, a short note about your goals and any crash or analytics reports you have. If you want a code review, we work as a collaborator on your repository, with read access only. For App Store Connect, a limited role is enough. We never need your passwords, and we do not ask you to share your Apple ID login.

Once you place your order, we reply with a short checklist and confirm the date of the call if your package includes one.
